doc.title: Grover Mitchell interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, February 13, 1996

chapter: Opening and the Basie band today
title: Returning to Basie in 1980 and helping the ailing leader
summary: Mitchell calls the band an apprenticeship, describes returning in 1980 when Basie was ill after strokes, and taking over as leader about nine months ago.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Oh, yeah. That’s a lesson that, well this band is kind of an apprenticeship for somebody like me. I’ve been in and out of this band for about 35 years, in one capacity or another. Most of my time I spent as lead trombone player. Then I came back in 1980 when the old man got sick, and I was helping. I was playing, but at the same time, you know I was starting to be his hands and arms and legs and I had to even help him think you know. Because he’d had a couple of strokes and all that, and he could get a little bit, you know that dementia that goes along with older people having strokes and everything. So it wasn’t, to me that I did so much for him but I learned so much having to behave like that with him, because he was a great man. You know? You’d have to be around him to really see, you know he was a great man. Yeah. He was a naturally great man.
I should explain to our viewers that you have taken over the Basie band, it’s about eight months now?
About nine. Yeah. It’s getting on towards a year. © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-
Well they seem to be in good hands.
Well thank you. I appreciate that.
